content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 12
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
25 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** and-they-sent and-called-him. And-Jeroboam and-all the-assembly-of Israel came and-spoke to-Rehoboam, saying,

**LOGOS (formal):** And they sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The people sent for him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly went to Rehoboam and said,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** "Your-father made-heavy ʾet-our-yoke. And-you now, lighten the-hard service-of your-father and-ʾet-his-heavy yoke that he-put upon-us, and-we-will-serve-you."

**LOGOS (formal):** "Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke on us, and we will serve you."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "Your father crushed us with heavy labor. Lighten the harsh demands and the heavy burden he placed on us, and we will serve you."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said to-them, "Go — yet three days — and-return to-me." And-the-people went.

**LOGOS (formal):** He said to them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people went away.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Rehoboam answered, "Come back in three days." So the people left.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Rehoboam consulted with the-elders who had-been standing before Solomon his-father while-he-was-alive, saying, "How do-you advise to-return a-word to-this people?"

**LOGOS (formal):** Then King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he was yet alive, saying, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Rehoboam consulted the older advisers who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. "What do you recommend?" he asked.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-they-spoke to-him, saying, "If today you-will-be a-servant to-this people and-serve-them and-answer-them and-speak to-them good words, then-they-will-be servants to-you all the-days."

**LOGOS (formal):** And they said to him, "If you will be a servant to this people today and serve them, and speak good words to them when you answer them, then they will be your servants forever."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** They replied, "If you will serve this people today — if you will be their servant, answer them well, and speak kindly to them — they will serve you forever."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** But-he-forsook ʾet-the-counsel-of the-elders that they-counseled-him, and-he-consulted with the-young-men who had-grown-up with-him, who-stood before-him.

**LOGOS (formal):** But he abandoned the counsel that the old men gave him and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and turned to the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said to-them, "What do-you advise, and-we-will-return a-word to-this people who-spoke to-me, saying, 'Lighten the-yoke that your-father put upon-us'?"

**LOGOS (formal):** And he said to them, "What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He asked them, "What do you suggest? How should we respond to these people who are asking me to lighten the burden my father put on them?"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-the-young-men who had-grown-up with-him spoke to-him, saying, "Thus you-shall-say to-this people who-spoke to-you, saying, 'Your-father made-heavy our-yoke, but-you lighten it for-us' — thus you-shall-speak to-them: 'My-little-finger is-thicker than-my-father's loins.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the young men who had grown up with him said to him, "Thus shall you speak to this people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us': 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The young men who had grown up with him replied, "This is what you should tell them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist!

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-now, my-father loaded upon-you a-heavy yoke, and-I will-add to your-yoke. My-father disciplined-you with-whips, but-I will-discipline-you with-scorpions.'"

**LOGOS (formal):** And now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** My father laid a heavy burden on you? I'll make it heavier! My father disciplined you with whips? I'll discipline you with barbed lashes!'"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-Jeroboam and-all the-people came to-Rehoboam on-the-third day, as the-king had-spoken, saying, "Return to-me on-the-third day."

**LOGOS (formal):** So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king said, "Come to me again the third day."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, as the king had instructed.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king answered ʾet-the-people harshly, and-forsook ʾet-the-counsel-of the-elders that they-counseled-him.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the king answered the people harshly, and forsaking the counsel that the old men had given him,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king answered the people harshly. Rejecting the advice of the elders,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-he-spoke to-them according-to-the-counsel-of the-young-men, saying, "My-father made-heavy your-yoke, and-I will-add to your-yoke. My-father disciplined-you with-whips, but-I will-discipline-you with-scorpions."

**LOGOS (formal):** he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** he spoke to them as the young men had advised: "My father made your burden heavy; I will make it heavier. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with barbed lashes."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king did-not listen to the-people, for it-was a-turning from YHWH, so-that he-might-establish ʾet-his-word that YHWH spoke by-the-hand-of Ahijah the-Shilonite to-Jeroboam son-of Nebat.

**LOGOS (formal):** So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD that he might fulfill his word, which the LORD spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king refused to listen to the people. This turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word he had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah of Shiloh.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-all Israel saw that the-king did-not listen to-them, and-the-people returned the-king a-word, saying, "What portion have-we in-David? And-there-is-no inheritance in-the-son-of Jesse! To-your-tents, Israel! Now see-to your-own-house, David!" And-Israel went to-their-tents.

**LOGOS (formal):** And when all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, "What portion do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, David." So Israel went to their tents.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen, the people shouted back: "What share do we have in David? We owe nothing to the son of Jesse! Go home, Israel! Look after your own house, David!" And the Israelites went home.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-the-sons-of Israel who-dwelt in-the-cities-of Judah — Rehoboam reigned over-them.

**LOGOS (formal):** But Rehoboam reigned over the people of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites living in the towns of Judah.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Rehoboam sent ʾet-Adoram, who was over the-forced-labor, and-all Israel stoned-him with-stones, and-he-died. And-the-king Rehoboam made-haste to-go-up into-the-chariot, to-flee to-Jerusalem.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was taskmaster over the forced labor, and all Israel stoned him to death with stones. And King Rehoboam hurried to mount his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely escaped by jumping into his chariot and racing back to Jerusalem.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 21
**EMET (literal):** And-Rehoboam came to-Jerusalem, and-he-assembled ʾet-all the-house-of Judah and-ʾet-the-tribe-of Benjamin — a-hundred and-eighty thousand chosen men, makers-of war — to-fight against the-house-of Israel, to-return the-kingdom to-Rehoboam son-of Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the entire fighting force of Judah and Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand warriors — to attack Israel and reclaim the kingdom.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** 'Thus says YHWH: You-shall-not go-up, and-you-shall-not fight against your-brothers the-sons-of Israel. Return each-man to-his-house, for from-me this thing has-happened.'" And-they-heard ʾet-the-word-of YHWH and-returned to-go, according-to-the-word-of YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** 'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up or fight against your brothers the people of Israel. Every man return to his home, for this thing is from me.'" So they listened to the word of the LORD and went home again, according to the word of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** 'This is what the LORD says: Do not attack your fellow Israelites. Everyone go home, because I am behind this.'" They obeyed the LORD's word and went home.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-Jeroboam built ʾet-Shechem in-the-hill-country-of Ephraim and-dwelt in-it. And-he-went-out from-there and-built ʾet-Penuel.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And he went out from there and built Penuel.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and made it his capital. He also fortified Penuel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** And-Jeroboam said in-his-heart, "Now the-kingdom will-return to-the-house-of David.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will turn back to the house of David.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But Jeroboam thought to himself, "The kingdom will eventually go back to David's house.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** If this people goes-up to-make sacrifices in-the-house-of YHWH in-Jerusalem, then-the-heart-of this people will-return to their-lord, to-Rehoboam king-of Judah, and-they-will-kill-me, and-return to Rehoboam king-of Judah."

**LOGOS (formal):** If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will turn again to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** If these people keep going up to the LORD's temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices, their loyalty will shift back to King Rehoboam of Judah. They'll kill me and return to him."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king took-counsel, and-made two calves-of gold. And-he-said to-them, "Too-much for-you, going-up to-Jerusalem. Behold your-gods, Israel, who brought-you-up from-the-land-of Egypt!"

**LOGOS (formal):** So the king took counsel and made two calves of gold. And he said to the people, "You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** After consulting his advisers, the king made two golden calves. He announced to the people, "You've been going to Jerusalem long enough! Here are your gods, Israel — the gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 30
**EMET (literal):** And-this thing became a-sin, and-the-people went before the-one, to Dan.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then this thing became a sin, for the people went as far as Dan to be before one.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And this became a terrible sin. The people traveled as far as Dan to worship before the calf there.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 31
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made ʾet-a-house-of high-places, and-he-made priests from-the-ends-of the-people who were not from-the-sons-of Levi.

**LOGOS (formal):** He also made houses on high places and appointed priests from among all the people, who were not of the Levites.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Jeroboam also built shrines on the hilltops and appointed anyone he wanted as priests — people who were not Levites.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** And-he-went-up upon the-altar that he-made in-Bethel on-the-fifteenth day in-the-eighth month, in-the-month that he-devised from-his-own-heart. And-he-made a-feast for-the-sons-of Israel, and-went-up upon the-altar to-burn-incense.

**LOGOS (formal):** He went up to the altar that he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the month that he had devised from his own heart. And he instituted a feast for the people of Israel and went up to the altar to make offerings.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** On the fifteenth day of the eighth month — a date he chose on his own authority — he went up to the altar he had built in Bethel. He established his own festival for the Israelites and went to the altar to burn incense.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
